title: sweep rule file
description: A sweep rule file: the version of the format and the rules it holds. Unknown fields are an error, so a typo is reported instead of being ignored.

description.description: What the rule cleans and what happens after it.

category.description: browsers, system, dev, apps, user or a category of your own.

risk.description: safe comes back on its own, moderate comes back at a cost, dangerous may still be wanted.

default_enabled.description: Whether the rule is part of the default profile.

tags.description: For profiles to select, such as dev.

requires_admin.description: Whether the rule needs administrator rights.

requires_closed.description: Processes that must not run, or the rule is skipped.

os_min_build.description: Oldest Windows build the rule runs on (10 1809 is 17763).

trash.description: Send to the recycle bin instead of deleting; on for dangerous rules unless it says otherwise.

path.description: Path with %VARS% and the glob masks *, ** and ?.

mode.description: contents (the default) clears what the path matched, self removes it, files takes only the files that match include.

include.description: Name masks to take, relative to path.

exclude.description: Name masks to leave alone, relative to path.

min_age_days.description: Take only what has not changed for this many days.

min_size.description: Take only files at least this big, such as 50MB; suffixes are powers of 1024.

cmd.description: Command to run, for kind: command.

args.description: Arguments of the command, for kind: command.
